items.title: Samples, days and diet
items.what: 10 stool samples from one person, one per day; days 1-5 high carbohydrate and high calorie, days 6-10 low carbohydrate and low calorie.
questions: Does a MAG, a gene or a motif differ between the two diet periods?

items.title: Read statistics per sample (our run)
items.what: Reads, bases, read N50 and read quality per sample after the read filter (Q 10 or more, 1 kb or longer), before and after adapter trimming: 166.5 Gbp went into the assembly.
questions: How much of each sample was sequenced, and how long and accurate were its reads?

items.title: A small sample of the reads themselves
items.what: 30,022 random raw reads from the ten samples (about 3,000 each), the 18,070 of them that passed the filter and trimming, and where the 27,427 raw reads that map sit on the assembly.
questions: What does a read look like before and after filtering?
How much of a read maps, and are some reads joins of two molecules?

items.title: Read QC of your own libraries
items.what: For each of the 10 student libraries: reads, bases, read N50, quality, a read length by quality histogram and the bases per hour of the run (42.2 Gbp of pass reads in the ten libraries), with the check that each library holds the right sample and a comparison with our first run of the same DNA.
questions: How did our library compare with the other groups' and with the first run of the same DNA?
Was the yield or the read length set by the sample or by the library prep?

items.title: The community seen by your library
items.what: 50,000 random reads from each student library mapped to the co-assembly: reads and bases per contig, so each library gives its own MAG abundance profile for its day (barcode01 is day 1, DNA01, and so on).
questions: Does a second library of the same DNA give the same MAG abundances, and which MAGs differ most?
How many reads are needed before rare MAGs show up?

items.title: The co-assembly
items.what: All 20,302 contigs (1.87 Gbp) as sequence, and a table with each contig's length, depth, GC, whether it is circular (401 are), its MAG and a taxonomy guess from the contig alone (Metabuli), useful for contigs outside MAGs.
questions: What is on the circular contigs that are not in a MAG (plasmids, phages)?

items.title: Depth of every contig on every day
items.what: Mean read depth of each contig in each of the 10 samples, from mapping all reads back to the assembly (columns 2-NP to 11-NP are DNA01 to DNA10; 1-NP is all samples pooled).
questions: Does a plasmid or phage contig rise and fall with its host MAG?

items.title: Assembly graph
items.what: The assembler's graph: 63,068 pieces of sequence and 2,535 links between them, showing where contigs could continue.
questions: Which contigs are connected to a MAG's contigs but were left out of it?

items.title: Possible misassemblies
items.what: 331 places in 191 contigs where the methylation pattern changes along the contig, a hint that two genomes were joined; 19 of them also have read evidence of a join (clipped reads, no reads across).
questions: Is a surprising gene in a MAG on a contig that may be a join?

items.title: MAG table: quality and taxonomy
items.what: 421 MAGs (257 high quality, 164 medium quality) with completeness, contamination, size, contigs, rRNA and tRNA genes, and the GTDB name with its closest reference genome.
questions: Which families dominate, and how complete are their genomes?

items.title: MAG abundance on each day
items.what: Share of each sample's bases on each of the 421 MAGs on each day, the change between the two diet periods, the same per phylum, and how different the days are (Bray-Curtis).
questions: Which MAGs or phyla change most between the diet periods?
Do MAGs with a shared trait rise or fall together?

items.title: MAG sequences
items.what: One FASTA file per MAG (421 files, in the folder binning/bins of mmlong2's table archive), for gene searches, comparisons or figures of a chosen genome.
questions: How similar are two MAGs of the same genus along their genomes?

items.title: Genes of every MAG (Bakta)
items.what: 1,017,373 protein-coding genes in all 421 MAGs, each with its position, name and the evidence for the name, plus rRNA and tRNA genes and resistance-gene matches (AMRFinderPlus). Only contigs in MAGs were annotated: contigs outside MAGs, such as most plasmids, have no gene table yet (they can be annotated: quick to compute).
questions: Which MAGs carry genes for a named function, such as a vitamin pathway or a toxin?
Where do resistance genes sit, and what is next to them?

items.title: Carbohydrate-active enzymes and fermentation genes
items.what: CAZyme families (dbCAN) and marker genes for butyrate, propionate and other products, computed for 17 MAGs: six that rise and six that fall between the diet periods (among the abundant high-quality MAGs), four stable ones and a control.
questions: Do MAGs that rise on the low-carbohydrate diet carry fewer starch-degrading enzymes?

items.title: The same searches on other MAGs, or for another gene family
items.what: Genes can be predicted in any MAG or contig (Pyrodigal) and searched with the CAZyme database (all dbCAN families) or the 30 selected KEGG marker genes, in minutes. Other gene families need their profiles downloaded first.
questions: Which of all MAGs can degrade a given fibre, or make a given product?

items.title: Methylation motifs of each MAG
items.what: 1,057 methylated motifs in 335 MAGs (Nanomotif): the sequence, the base and type (6mA, 5mC, 4mC) and how often the motif's sites are methylated.
questions: Do related MAGs share motifs, and which MAGs have none?

items.title: Methylation of every motif on every contig
items.what: For 8,427 contigs and 896 motifs: sites and the share methylated, also in 12,529 windows of about 100 kb along long contigs.
questions: Does a plasmid carry the methylation pattern of a MAG, and so likely live in it?

items.title: Contigs placed in MAGs by methylation
items.what: All 8,427 contigs with a mean depth of 5 or more compared with every MAG's motifs. 2,072 matched one MAG: 1,175 contigs outside MAGs, 789 contigs in their own MAG (a check) and 108 in a different MAG. Module 6 shows how often depth and composition agree.
questions: Which MAG hosts a given plasmid or phage?

items.title: Sequence variants within MAGs
items.what: 590,588 variant positions that passed the filter, found by mapping the reads back to the contigs, and the share of variable positions per contig and per MAG (in the contig and MAG tables): a sign of strain mixtures.
questions: Which MAGs are mixtures of strains, and are they the abundant ones?

items.title: New statistics and figures from these tables
items.what: Anything that combines the tables above: correlations, diversity per day, ordinations, gene neighbourhood maps, a comparison of chosen MAGs. Minutes on a laptop.
questions: Do butyrate-producing MAGs fall on the low-carbohydrate diet?

items.title: Anything that needs all the reads again
items.what: Methylation or depth at single-read level in a region, mapping reads to a new reference, re-assembling or re-binning, or following strains along reads. The full reads (about 186 Gbp) are only on the server; such a job takes hours and is not part of the group reports.

items.title: Not measured in this study
items.what: Gene expression (RNA), metabolites, cell counts or absolute abundance, health data, other people, or more than ten days. Sequencing gives each MAG's share of the DNA, not how many cells there were or what they were doing.
